gloss: (baseball) walk; base on balls; four balls

definitions.explanation: In baseball, the situation in which the batter is awarded first base after the pitcher throws four pitches outside the strike zone (balls). The Japanese term is a wasei-eigo coinage from English "four" + "ball" — in real English baseball usage this is called a "walk" or "base on balls."

examples.japanese: フォアボール⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{出塁|しゅつるい}→出塁：09486_shutsurui⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He got on base with a walk.

examples.japanese: ⟦ピッチャー→ピッチャー：09482_picchaa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧フォアボール⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}して→出す：01087_dasu⟧しまった。
examples.english: The pitcher gave up a walk.

examples.japanese: {満塁|まんるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧フォアボール⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{一点|いってん}→一点：08894_itten⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: A bases-loaded walk brought in a run.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ピッチャー→ピッチャー：09482_picchaa⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦コントロール→コントロール：10861_kontorooru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}く→悪い：00908_warui⟧、フォアボール⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{連発|れんぱつ}した→連発する：21028_renpatsusuru⟧。
examples.english: Today's pitcher had poor control and gave up walks one after another.

notes:
フォアボール is a wasei-eigo (Japanese-made English) term combining "four" + "ball." The official term in Japanese baseball rules is {四球|しきゅう}, but in everyday speech and broadcasts フォアボール is far more common. In English baseball, the equivalent expressions are "a walk" or "a base on balls" (BB) — never "four balls."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- フォアボール⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{出塁|しゅつるい}→出塁：09486_shutsurui⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to get on base with a walk
- フォアボール⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧: (pitcher) to give up a walk
- フォアボール⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}ぶ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧: (batter) to draw a walk (literally "choose a walk" — i.e. lay off bad pitches)
- フォアボール⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{連発|れんぱつ}する→連発する：21028_renpatsusuru⟧: to give up walks repeatedly
- {満塁|まんるい}フォアボール / {押|お}し{出|だ}し⟦の→の：09472_no⟧フォアボール: bases-loaded walk that forces in a run

RELATED WORDS:
- {四球|しきゅう}: walk / base on balls (the formal/written term)
- デッド⟦ボール→ボール：00017_booru⟧: hit by pitch (also wasei-eigo; English uses "hit by pitch" / HBP)
- ⟦ストライク→ストライク：25892_sutoraiku⟧: strike
- ⟦ボール→ボール：00017_booru⟧: ball (a pitch outside the strike zone)
- ⟦{三振|さんしん}→三振：08588_sanshin⟧: strikeout
- ⟦{敬遠|けいえん}→敬遠：12930_keien⟧: intentional walk

USAGE:
- The verb pairs with the agent: a pitcher "gives up" a walk (フォアボール⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧) while a batter "draws / takes" a walk (フォアボール⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}ぶ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧).
- Despite the name, only four balls (without three strikes first) are needed; the count goes up to a maximum of three balls and two strikes before the fourth ball results in a walk.
